lean.statement: Let X be a measurable space and mu a nonzero sigma-finite measure on X. Let f and g be real-valued functions on X. Assume f is measurable, exp(f) and exp(g) are integrable with respect to mu, and the function r(x) = f(x) - log(integral exp(f) dmu) - g(x) + log(integral exp(g) dmu) is integrable with respect to the normalized exponential tilt mu.tilted f. Then the extended-nonnegative-real Kullback-Leibler divergence klDiv(mu.tilted f, mu.tilted g) is not infinity, and its real value equals the integral of r with respect to mu.tilted f.
approved_definition_context: For an integrable exponential weight exp(h), mu.tilted h denotes the probability measure obtained by normalizing exp(h) against the common base measure mu.
InformationTheory.klDiv is extended-nonnegative-real valued. The assertion that it is not top is a separate finiteness certificate; toReal alone would not preserve that information.
The displayed explicit ratio is a real-valued representative. Its integrability is assumed under the left normalized tilt, not merely under the base measure.
